claim: Memory B (Bmem) cells in mice can be divided into two subpopulations: CD80hi Bmem cells and CD80lo Bmem cells.
source: In mice, memory B (Bmem) cells can be divided into two subpopulations: CD80hi Bmem cells, which preferentially differentiate into plasma cells; and CD80lo Bmem cells, which become germinal center (GC) B cells during a recall response.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: CD80hi Bmem cells preferentially differentiate into plasma cells during a recall response.
source: In mice, memory B (Bmem) cells can be divided into two subpopulations: CD80hi Bmem cells, which preferentially differentiate into plasma cells; and CD80lo Bmem cells, which become germinal center (GC) B cells during a recall response.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: CD80lo Bmem cells become germinal center (GC) B cells during a recall response.
source: In mice, memory B (Bmem) cells can be divided into two subpopulations: CD80hi Bmem cells, which preferentially differentiate into plasma cells; and CD80lo Bmem cells, which become germinal center (GC) B cells during a recall response.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The distinct responses of CD80hi and CD80lo Bmem cells can be B-cell-intrinsic and essentially independent of B-cell receptor (BCR) isotypes.
source: We demonstrate that these distinct responses can be B-cell-intrinsic and essentially independent of B-cell receptor (BCR) isotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro culture experiments shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The development of CD80hi Bmem cells in the primary immune response requires follicular helper T cells.
source: Furthermore, we find that the development of CD80hi Bmem cells in the primary immune response requires follicular helper T cells, a relatively strong CD40 signal and a high-affinity BCR on B cells, whereas the development of CD80lo Bmem cells does not.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using CD4+ T-cell-specific BCL6-deficient mice shown in Figure 1c,d.

claim: The development of CD80hi Bmem cells in the primary immune response requires a relatively strong CD40 signal.
source: Furthermore, we find that the development of CD80hi Bmem cells in the primary immune response requires follicular helper T cells, a relatively strong CD40 signal and a high-affinity BCR on B cells, whereas the development of CD80lo Bmem cells does not.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with anti-CD40L blocking antibody and agonistic anti-CD40 antibody shown in Figure 2.

claim: The development of CD80hi Bmem cells in the primary immune response requires a high-affinity BCR on B cells.
source: Furthermore, we find that the development of CD80hi Bmem cells in the primary immune response requires follicular helper T cells, a relatively strong CD40 signal and a high-affinity BCR on B cells, whereas the development of CD80lo Bmem cells does not.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using B1-8hi ki and B1-8 ki mice shown in Figure 5.

claim: The development of CD80lo Bmem cells does not require follicular helper T cells, strong CD40 signal, or high-affinity BCR.
source: Furthermore, we find that the development of CD80hi Bmem cells in the primary immune response requires follicular helper T cells, a relatively strong CD40 signal and a high-affinity BCR on B cells, whereas the development of CD80lo Bmem cells does not.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing CD80lo Bmem cells are less affected by TFH cell deficiency or CD40L blocking.

claim: Quantitative differences in CD40 stimulation are sufficient to recapitulate the distinct B cell fate decisions in an in vitro culture system.
source: Quantitative differences in CD40 stimulation were enough to recapitulate the distinct B cell fate decisions in an in vitro culture system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using 40LB feeder cells with different CD40L expression levels shown in Figure 3.

claim: The quantity of CD40 signaling is translated into NF-κB activation.
source: The quantity of CD40 signaling appears to be translated into NF-κB activation, followed by BATF upregulation that promotes Bmem cell differentiation from GC B cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments showing NF-κB nuclear translocation and knockdown experiments in Figure 6.

claim: NF-κB activation is followed by BATF upregulation that promotes Bmem cell differentiation from GC B cells.
source: The quantity of CD40 signaling appears to be translated into NF-κB activation, followed by BATF upregulation that promotes Bmem cell differentiation from GC B cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments showing BATF expression and overexpression in Figure 7.

claim: The majority of CD80hi Bmem cells expressed PD-L2 and CD73.
source: Consistent with these reports, most of the CD80hi Bmem cells expressed PD-L2 and CD73, thus constituting the reported affinity-matured subset (He et al., 2017; Tomayko et al., 2010; Zuccarino-Catania et al., 2014), whereas the CD80lo Bmem cells consisted of PD-L2+ and PD-L2−, as well as CD73+ and CD73− subpopulations (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: CD80lo Bmem cells consisted of PD-L2+ and PD-L2− subpopulations.
source: Consistent with these reports, most of the CD80hi Bmem cells expressed PD-L2 and CD73, thus constituting the reported affinity-matured subset (He et al., 2017; Tomayko et al., 2010; Zuccarino-Catania et al., 2014), whereas the CD80lo Bmem cells consisted of PD-L2+ and PD-L2−, as well as CD73+ and CD73− subpopulations (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: CD80lo Bmem cells consisted of CD73+ and CD73− subpopulations.
source: Consistent with these reports, most of the CD80hi Bmem cells expressed PD-L2 and CD73, thus constituting the reported affinity-matured subset (He et al., 2017; Tomayko et al., 2010; Zuccarino-Catania et al., 2014), whereas the CD80lo Bmem cells consisted of PD-L2+ and PD-L2−, as well as CD73+ and CD73− subpopulations (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The majority of CD80hi Bmem cells express a lower level of CD62L.
source: Although CD62L was reported to be expressed on Bmem cells (Anderson et al., 2007), the majority of CD80hi Bmem cells express a lower level of CD62L (a phenotype that somewhat resembles TEM cells), whereas most CD80lo Bmem cells express a higher level of CD62L (a phenotype that somewhat resembles TCM cells).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Most CD80lo Bmem cells express a higher level of CD62L.
source: Although CD62L was reported to be expressed on Bmem cells (Anderson et al., 2007), the majority of CD80hi Bmem cells express a lower level of CD62L (a phenotype that somewhat resembles TEM cells), whereas most CD80lo Bmem cells express a higher level of CD62L (a phenotype that somewhat resembles TCM cells).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Both CD80hi and CD80lo Bmem cells expressed FAS at a higher level than naïve B cells.
source: Both CD80hi and CD80lo Bmem cells expressed FAS (also called CD95 or APO1) at a higher level than naïve B cells, as previously reported (Anderson et al., 2007), but at a lower level than GC B cells, and, as expected, they were GL7–.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Both CD80hi and CD80lo Bmem cells expressed FAS at a lower level than GC B cells.
source: Both CD80hi and CD80lo Bmem cells expressed FAS (also called CD95 or APO1) at a higher level than naïve B cells, as previously reported (Anderson et al., 2007), but at a lower level than GC B cells, and, as expected, they were GL7–.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: CD80hi and CD80lo Bmem cells were GL7 negative.
source: Both CD80hi and CD80lo Bmem cells expressed FAS (also called CD95 or APO1) at a higher level than naïve B cells, as previously reported (Anderson et al., 2007), but at a lower level than GC B cells, and, as expected, they were GL7–.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The number of CD80hi Bmem cells decreased by approximately ten-fold in Cd4-Cre Bcl6f/f mice compared to control mice.
source: Six weeks after immunization, the number of CD80hi Bmem cells decreased by approximately ten-fold in Cd4-Cre Bcl6f/f mice as compared to the control Cd4-Cre Bcl6+/+ mice, while the number of CD80lo Bmem cells was essentially unchanged (Figure 1c,d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1c,d.

claim: The number of CD80lo Bmem cells was essentially unchanged in Cd4-Cre Bcl6f/f mice compared to control mice.
source: Six weeks after immunization, the number of CD80hi Bmem cells decreased by approximately ten-fold in Cd4-Cre Bcl6f/f mice as compared to the control Cd4-Cre Bcl6+/+ mice, while the number of CD80lo Bmem cells was essentially unchanged (Figure 1c,d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1c,d.

claim: TFH cells express CD40L at a markedly higher level than naïve or effector T cells.
source: TFH cells differ from naïve or effecter CD4+ T cells in that they express a much higher level of CD40L (Breitfeld et al., 2000), as we confirmed using purified T-cell subsets (Figure 2a and Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Stimulation of B cells through CD40, but not BCR, induced CD80 expression in a time- and dose-dependent manner.
source: As previously indicated (Lenschow et al., 1994; Ranheim and Kipps, 1993), stimulation of B cells through CD40, but not BCR, induced CD80 expression in a time- and dose-dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1b,c.

claim: CD40L-mediated stimulation is indispensable for Bmem cell development.
source: After immunization of such mice, however, Bmem cell development from the donor B cells was abrogated altogether in the absence of CD40L, indicating that CD40L-mediated stimulation is indispensable for Bmem cell development (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data using CD40L-deficient mice shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Treatment with anti-CD40L blocking antibody preferentially affected CD80hi Bmem cell development.
source: This treatment preferentially affected CD80hi Bmem cell development. At 10 days after immunization, the frequency of CD80hi Bmem cells was significantly reduced among class-switched Bmem cells, of which ~90% were IgG1+ and ~10% were IgM– IgG1–, both normally containing the CD80hi cells at a similar frequency (Figure 2c,d and Figure 2—figure supplement 1f–h).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c,d.

claim: Administration of agonistic anti-CD40 Ab to immunized mice markedly increased the frequency and the number of CD80hi Bmem cells.
source: As an opposite experiment, administration of agonistic anti-CD40 Ab to immunized mice markedly increased the frequency and the number of CD80hi Bmem cells, while the numbers of CD80lo Bmem cells, GC B cells and plasmablasts remained unchanged (Figure 2e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e,f.

claim: The numbers of CD80lo Bmem cells, GC B cells and plasmablasts remained unchanged after administration of agonistic anti-CD40 Ab.
source: As an opposite experiment, administration of agonistic anti-CD40 Ab to immunized mice markedly increased the frequency and the number of CD80hi Bmem cells, while the numbers of CD80lo Bmem cells, GC B cells and plasmablasts remained unchanged (Figure 2e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e,f.

claim: The frequency of CD80hi Bmem cells was significantly lower in mice that had received CD40L-knockdown T cells compared to control T cells.
source: Among the generated donor-derived class-switched Bmem cells, the frequency of CD80hi Bmem cells was significantly lower in mice that had received the CD40L-knockdown T cells as compared to those that had received the control T cells (Figure 2g–i and Figure 2—figure supplement 1i).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2g–i.

claim: B cells cultured on 40LB-hi expressed the highest level of CD80.
source: As expected, B cells cultured on 40LB-hi (iGB-hi cells) expressed the highest level of CD80, whereas those on 40LB-mid (iGB-mid cells) or 40LB-lo (iGB-lo cells) exhibited intermediate or the lowest levels of CD80 expression, respectively (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: iGB-lo cells expressed Fas at a lower level than iGB-hi and iGB-mid cells.
source: It is of note that the iGB-lo cells expressed Fas at a lower level than iGB-hi and iGB-mid cells, whereas they expressed CD38 and CD62L at higher levels than iGB-hi and iGB-mid cells, perhaps reflecting their relatively lower activation status (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: iGB-lo cells expressed CD38 and CD62L at higher levels than iGB-hi and iGB-mid cells.
source: It is of note that the iGB-lo cells expressed Fas at a lower level than iGB-hi and iGB-mid cells, whereas they expressed CD38 and CD62L at higher levels than iGB-hi and iGB-mid cells, perhaps reflecting their relatively lower activation status (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: iMB cells derived from iGB-hi cells (iMB-hi cells) contained almost exclusively CD80hi cells.
source: However, the iMB cells derived from iGB-hi cells (iMB-hi cells) contained almost exclusively CD80hi cells, whereas iMB cells from iGB-lo cells (iMB-lo cells) were dominated by CD80lo cells, irrespective of their BCR isotypes (IgG1+ or IgG1–). iMB cells derived from iGB-mid cells exhibited an intermediate phenotype (Figure 3d,e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3d,e.

claim: iMB cells from iGB-lo cells (iMB-lo cells) were dominated by CD80lo cells.
source: However, the iMB cells derived from iGB-hi cells (iMB-hi cells) contained almost exclusively CD80hi cells, whereas iMB cells from iGB-lo cells (iMB-lo cells) were dominated by CD80lo cells, irrespective of their BCR isotypes (IgG1+ or IgG1–). iMB cells derived from iGB-mid cells exhibited an intermediate phenotype (Figure 3d,e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3d,e.

claim: iMB-hi cells expressed PD-L2, CD73 and FAS at higher levels than iMB-lo cells.
source: In addition, iMB-hi cells expressed PD-L2, CD73 and FAS at higher levels than iMB-lo cells, whereas both expressed equally low levels of GL7 (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: Both iMB-hi and iMB-lo cells expressed equally low levels of GL7.
source: In addition, iMB-hi cells expressed PD-L2, CD73 and FAS at higher levels than iMB-lo cells, whereas both expressed equally low levels of GL7 (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: iGB-hi cells grow far more extensively than iGB-lo cells beyond two days of culture.
source: iGB-hi cells grow far more extensively than iGB-lo cells beyond two days of culture (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: The bifurcated Bmem cell fate was not determined by different levels of cell proliferation.
source: These data indicate that the bifurcated Bmem cell fate was not determined by different levels of cell proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experiments using day 2 iGB cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1e,f.

claim: The duration of CD40 signaling may affect the development of CD80hi Bmem cells.
source: However, they also demonstrated that the frequency of the CD80hi population in iMB-hi cells increased as the culture period of iGB-hi cells became longer (i.e. from 1 to 2 to 4 days), thus indicating that the duration of CD40 signaling may also affect the development of CD80hi Bmem cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1f,g.

claim: The addition of IL-21 to the iGB-hi and iGB-lo cell culture did not affect the frequencies of CD80hi iMB cells derived from each type of iGB cells.
source: Although IL-21 is a hallmark TFH cytokine, which is known to support GC B cell proliferation, the addition of IL-21 to the iGB-hi and iGB-lo cell culture did not affect the frequencies of CD80hi iMB cells derived from each type of iGB cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1h,i), suggesting that the contribution of IL-21 to the differential Bmem cell fate decision in vivo is less likely.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1h,i.

claim: iMB-lo cells preferentially differentiated toward GC B cells in culture.
source: Regardless of their BCR isotype, iMB-lo cells preferentially differentiated toward GC B cells, as clearly seen on day 2, whereas iMB-hi cells preferentially differentiated into plasmablasts or PCs, becoming evident on day 3. The behavior of the iMB-mid cells was intermediate (Figure 4a,b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4a,b.

claim: iMB-hi cells preferentially differentiated into plasmablasts or PCs in culture.
source: Regardless of their BCR isotype, iMB-lo cells preferentially differentiated toward GC B cells, as clearly seen on day 2, whereas iMB-hi cells preferentially differentiated into plasmablasts or PCs, becoming evident on day 3. The behavior of the iMB-mid cells was intermediate (Figure 4a,b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4a,b.

claim: Four days after immunization, most donor-derived, NP-binding plasmablasts were derived from iMB-hi cells.
source: Four days after immunization, most donor-derived, NP-binding plasmablasts were derived from iMB-hi cells. By contrast, the vast majority of donor-derived, NP-binding GC B and Bmem cells at day 10 were found to originate from iMB-lo cells (Figure 4e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4e,f.

claim: The vast majority of donor-derived, NP-binding GC B and Bmem cells at day 10 were found to originate from iMB-lo cells.
source: Four days after immunization, most donor-derived, NP-binding plasmablasts were derived from iMB-hi cells. By contrast, the vast majority of donor-derived, NP-binding GC B and Bmem cells at day 10 were found to originate from iMB-lo cells (Figure 4e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4e,f.

claim: CD40L expression on T cells was rapidly induced and its levels positively correlated with antigen dose.
source: CD40L expression on the T cells was rapidly induced and its levels positively correlated with antigen dose (Figure 5b), as was also the case for CD80 expression on B cells on day 2 (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: CD80 expression on B cells positively correlated with antigen dose.
source: CD40L expression on the T cells was rapidly induced and its levels positively correlated with antigen dose (Figure 5b), as was also the case for CD80 expression on B cells on day 2 (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: CD80 induction on B cells was suppressed by blocking with anti-CD40L mAb.
source: This CD80 induction was suppressed by blocking with anti-CD40L mAb, confirming that the CD40L–CD40 interaction leads to CD80 induction on B cells (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: IgG1+ Bmem cells developed from B1-8hi ki B cells contained a higher frequency of CD80hi cells than those from B1-8 ki B cells.
source: FCM analysis on day 7 after the immunization revealed that IgG1+ Bmem cells developed from B1-8hi ki B cells contained a higher frequency of CD80hi cells than those from B1-8 ki B cells (Figure 5e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5e,f.

claim: Among donor-derived Igλ+ or IgG1+ Bmem cells, those stained more brightly with NPmed (NPmedhi) contained a higher frequency of CD80hi Bmem cells than those stained less brightly (NPmedlo).
source: Among donor-derived Igλ+ or IgG1+ Bmem cells, those stained more brightly with NPmed (NPmedhi) contained a higher frequency of CD80hi Bmem cells than those stained less brightly (NPmedlo) (Figure 5g–j).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5g–j.

claim: CA-IKKβ, an activator of the canonical NF-κB pathway, upregulated CD80 expression on iGB-lo cells.
source: In accord with these data, among the constitutively active (CA) forms of protein kinases that are known to be activated by CD40 stimulation, CA-IKKβ, an activator of the canonical NF-κB pathway (Mercurio et al., 1997), but not CA-Akt or CA-MKK4, upregulated CD80 expression on iGB-lo cells (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: CA-Akt did not upregulate CD80 expression on iGB-lo cells.
source: In accord with these data, among the constitutively active (CA) forms of protein kinases that are known to be activated by CD40 stimulation, CA-IKKβ, an activator of the canonical NF-κB pathway (Mercurio et al., 1997), but not CA-Akt or CA-MKK4, upregulated CD80 expression on iGB-lo cells (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: CA-MKK4 did not upregulate CD80 expression on iGB-lo cells.
source: In accord with these data, among the constitutively active (CA) forms of protein kinases that are known to be activated by CD40 stimulation, CA-IKKβ, an activator of the canonical NF-κB pathway (Mercurio et al., 1997), but not CA-Akt or CA-MKK4, upregulated CD80 expression on iGB-lo cells (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Stimulation of splenic B cells with a higher concentration (10 μg/ml), but not a lower concentration (1 μg/ml), of anti-CD40 Ab induced the nuclear translocation of the NF-κB subunits c-Rel and RelA.
source: Stimulation of splenic B cells with a higher concentration (10 μg/ml), but not a lower concentration (1 μg/ml), of anti-CD40 Ab induced the nuclear translocation of the NF-κB subunits c-Rel and RelA (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Knockdown of Rel and Rela gene expression in iGB-hi cells resulted in downregulation of surface CD80 expression.
source: Furthermore, knockdown of Rel and Rela gene expression in iGB-hi cells resulted in downregulation of surface CD80 expression (Figure 6c,d and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6c,d.

claim: c-Rel- and Rela-knockdown iGB-hi cells generated fewer CD80hi iMB cells than mock-treated iGB-hi cells in vivo.
source: By using the iGB cell system, we showed that c-Rel- and Rela-knockdown iGB-hi cells generated fewer CD80hi iMB cells than mock-treated iGB-hi cells in vivo (Figure 6c–f and Figure 6—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6c–f.

claim: The knockdown of Rela selectively suppressed the development of CD80hi Bmem cells among the B cells that had responded to an immunized antigen.
source: Furthermore, we transferred NP-specific B cells transduced with the Rela-knockdown vector or a mock vector into mice, which were then immunized with NP-CGG. The knockdown of Rela selectively suppressed the development of CD80hi Bmem cells among the B cells that had responded to an immunized antigen (Figure 6g,h and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6g,h.

claim: CD40 stimulation induces IRF4 in B cells.
source: It has been observed that CD40 stimulation induces IRF4 in B cells and that bone marrow-derived dendritic cells from IRF4-deficient mice express a reduced level of CD80 upon LPS stimulation (Saito et al., 2007; Suzuki et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: IRF4 expression was upregulated by a high dose of anti-CD40 or anti-BCR Abs.
source: When ex-vivo GC B cells were cultured with anti-CD40 or anti-BCR Abs, of either high or low doses, or with various cytokines, IRF4 expression was found to be upregulated by a high dose of anti-CD40 or anti-BCR Abs, whereas BATF expression was selectively upregulated by a high dose of anti-CD40 Ab (Figure 7a,b and Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7a,b.

claim: BATF expression was selectively upregulated by a high dose of anti-CD40 Ab.
source: When ex-vivo GC B cells were cultured with anti-CD40 or anti-BCR Abs, of either high or low doses, or with various cytokines, IRF4 expression was found to be upregulated by a high dose of anti-CD40 or anti-BCR Abs, whereas BATF expression was selectively upregulated by a high dose of anti-CD40 Ab (Figure 7a,b and Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7a,b.

claim: Induced activation of BATF selectively upregulated CD80 expression in iGB-lo cells.
source: Induced activation of BATF selectively upregulated CD80 expression in iGB-lo cells, although IRF4 alone did not, and co-activation of BATF and IRF4 slightly enhanced CD80 expression (Figure 7c and Figure 7—figure supplement 1b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: IRF4 alone did not upregulate CD80 expression in iGB-lo cells.
source: Induced activation of BATF selectively upregulated CD80 expression in iGB-lo cells, although IRF4 alone did not, and co-activation of BATF and IRF4 slightly enhanced CD80 expression (Figure 7c and Figure 7—figure supplement 1b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Co-activation of BATF and IRF4 slightly enhanced CD80 expression in iGB-lo cells.
source: Induced activation of BATF selectively upregulated CD80 expression in iGB-lo cells, although IRF4 alone did not, and co-activation of BATF and IRF4 slightly enhanced CD80 expression (Figure 7c and Figure 7—figure supplement 1b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: A BATF mutant (BATF-HKE), which is defective in IRF4 binding, failed to upregulate CD80 expression regardless of exogenous IRF4.
source: In addition, a BATF mutant (BATF- HKE), which is defective in IRF4 binding (Tussiwand et al., 2012), failed to upregulate CD80 expression regardless of exogenous IRF4 (Figure 7d), suggesting that the exogenous BATF formed a heterodimer with endogenous IRF4 for CD80 upregulation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7d.

claim: An IKKβ inhibitor suppressed CD40-induced expression of CD80 as well as of BATF and IRF4.
source: As an IKKβ inhibitor suppressed CD40-induced expression of CD80 as well as of BATF and IRF4, the canonical NF-κB pathway appears to upregulate the expression of BATF and IRF4 (Figure 7e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: GL7+ Efnb1+ CD38+ GC-derived memory precursors (pre-Bmem) cells expressed BATF and CD80 at higher levels than GL7+ Efnb1+ CD38− GC B cells at 10 days after immunization.
source: This idea was supported by our finding that GL7+ Efnb1+ CD38+ GC-derived memory precursors (pre-Bmem) cells (Laidlaw et al., 2017) expressed BATF and CD80 at higher levels than GL7+ Efnb1+ CD38− GC B cells at 10 days after immunization (Figure 7f,g and Figure 7—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7f,g.

claim: ERT2-BATF-expressing (GFP+) iMB cells contained a significantly higher proportion of CD80hi cells than mock-transduced iMB cells.
source: On the other hand, ERT2-BATF-expressing (GFP+) iMB cells were present and contained a significantly higher proportion of CD80hi cells than mock-transduced iMB cells (Figure 7i,j and Figure 7—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7i,j.

claim: The relatively long cytoplasmic tail of mIgG contains specific motifs that recruit signaling molecules such as Grb2 and SAP97 after BCR cross-linking.
source: The relatively long cytoplasmic tail of mIgG, as compared to that of membrane-bound IgM (mIgM) which consists of only three amino acids, contains specific motifs that recruit signaling molecules such as Grb2 and SAP97 after BCR cross-linking; these motifs and molecules are required for enhanced BCR signaling and plasma cell (PC) formation upon rechallenge (Engels et al., 2009; Kaisho et al., 1997; Liu et al., 2012; Lutz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: Naïve B cells expressing NP-specific mIgG1 expanded to a similar extent as NP-specific IgM+ naïve B cells upon primary immunization.
source: At odds with this model is the finding that naïve B cells expressing NP-specific mIgG1, which were derived from cloned mice generated from a single IgG1+ Bmem cell, expanded to a similar extent as NP-specific (IgH-knock-in) IgM+ naïve B cells, and both B cell types predominantly differentiated into GC B cells rather than PCs upon primary immunization (Kometani et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Human Bmem cells differentiate into PCs better than do naïve B cells in antigen-free in vitro cultures.
source: In support of this notion, human Bmem cells differentiate into PCs better than do naïve B cells in antigen-free in vitro cultures (Arpin et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: CD80+ PD-L2+ Bmem cells are prone to differentiate into PCs.
